name: dependency-risk-scanner
description: Tells you which of your repositories are exposed to a dependency advisory you paste (a CVE or GHSA id with the package, ecosystem, affected range and fixed version, or a deprecation notice). It reads the manifests and lockfiles of the repositories you name (or an owner's), and says per repository which version is declared or resolved and whether it is affected, may resolve to an affected version, is not affected, or is unknown. Version and range matching is done in code, never guessed. For one repository it can open an upgrade pull request that bumps the version in the manifest, writing each step (branch, commit, PR) only after you approve that one step. It never fetches advisories itself, runs installs, edits lockfiles or merges.

skills.name: Dependency exposure scan
skills.description: Which repositories declare a package named in an advisory, at which declared and resolved versions, and whether each is inside the affected range (computed in code); then an upgrade pull request for one repository, each write approved on its own card.
examples: CVE-2026-1234 affects lodash (npm) <4.17.21, fixed in 4.17.21: which of acme/web, acme/api use it?
Is acme/api exposed to this advisory? <paste the advisory>
Open the upgrade PR for acme/web
